units.citation: (2017). Restauration de la productivité des sols tropicaux et méditerranéens. .
units.quote:
Par ailleurs, l’aménagement des fonds de ravines ralentit les crues lors des 
averses cycloniques et protège les plaines et villes des inondations brutales 
et de l’envasement des barrages. (English: Furthermore, treating the ravine floors slows floods during cyclonic storms and protects plains and towns from sudden floods and dam siltation.)

relationship.outcome_raw: treated ravine floors slow cyclonic-storm floods and protect downstream plains and towns

context.practice_as_described: Masonry and gabion check dams (seuils imperméables en gabions ou en maçonnerie de gros blocs avec mortier): eleven impermeable sills built across medium ravines of a 49 ha catchment where water was critical at the end of the dry season, sometimes with stilling basins or wells, to trap organic-rich sediment, infiltrate runoff and store water for irrigation and livestock; the trapped "fonds frais" are then cropped intensively (banana, malanga, yam, fruit trees, sugar cane, vegetables) with manure and residues (pp568-569). BASELINE: untreated ravines (implied).
context.note: Chapter 42 (Brochet, Clossy, Lilin, Roose), "Amenagements hydro-agricoles : capture des eaux et restauration de la productivite des sols - cas du bassin de Gros Morne en Haiti", PDF pp566-580. Development-project monitoring (SOS ESF); no research plots or soil analyses (p577); figures from annual monitoring reports (Brochet 2012). Assertion, no measurement; the conclusion (p579) hedges: "Il a probablement réduit aussi les crues". The authors add the main effect is to spread floods and reduce their shear and sediment transport.

units.citation: Bullock et al. (2003). The role of wetlands in the hydrological cycle. Hydrology and Earth System Sciences.
units.quote:
Many wetlands exist because they overlie impermeable 
soils or rocks and there is little interaction with 
groundwater. The database contains 69 statements 
referring to groundwater recharge; 32 conclude merely 
that recharge takes place, and 18 conclude there is no 
recharge. There are similar numbers of studies that 
report wetlands either to recharge more (6) or less than 
(9) other land types. Some wetlands, such as floodplains 
in India and West Africa on sandy soils, recharge 
groundwater when flooded.

relationship.outcome_raw: wetlands recharge groundwater more than other land types in 6 studies

context.practice_as_described: EXISTING freshwater wetlands of all hydrological types (floodplain and headwater; lakes excluded, p2). No intervention: studies of what existing wetlands do. BASELINE: other land types or non-wetland parts of the catchment (forest, savannah grassland, arable land), or the catchment without the wetland.
context.note: Vote count of functional statements from the review's database (Table 5, pp7-8, 'number of functional statements for each wetland type'); the table's OCR is not in row/column order, so the counts are taken from the Conclusions text. A count of studies is not an effect size: strength unspecified. The authors warn (p5) that counts are not inter-compared, that some functions are studied more than others, and that the sample is dominated by North America. Comparator existing_wetland: home family per comparator_policy, out of the roll-up. Only the comparison with other land types is an effect (more 6 / less 9). The 32 'recharge takes place' and 18 'no recharge' statements describe presence of a process with no counterfactual (catalogue #28) and are not encoded. Mechanism in the quote: many wetlands overlie impermeable soils or rocks with little groundwater interaction; floodplains on sandy soils (India, West Africa) recharge when flooded.

units.quote:
There is strong evidence that wetlands evaporate more 
water that other land types, such as forests, savannah 
grassland or arable land. Two thirds of studies (48 of 
74) conclude that wetlands increase average annual 
evaporation or reduce average annual river flow. About 
10% of studies (7) conclude the opposite; for example 
some woodlands in Zambia had greater evaporation than 
the adjacent wetlands. The remaining 25% are neutral. 
There is no obvious distinction amongst different 
wetland sub-types or geographical regions of the world.

context.note: Global model (PNAS 2026; restoration explicitly modelled): van Zelst XBeach wave-attenuation lookup + EuroTop dike overtopping on 495,361 shore-normal transects, GLOFRIS coastal flood risk at ~1 km, GTSR surge enriched with IBTrACS cyclones (p8). units.citation: Kiptot et al. (2011). Gender and agroforestry in Africa: a review of women’s participation. Agroforestry Systems.
units.quote: In studies conducted by Epaphra (2001) in Tanzania and Gerhardt and Nemarundwe (2006) in Zimbabwe, it was noted that over 60% of women in Tanzania are responsible for managing tree species planted on farms while over 80% in Zimbabwe are responsible for watering young seedlings. This trend is conﬁrmed by Franzel et al. (2002a) in a study undertaken in Embu, Kenya to determine early stages of adoption of calliandra fodder in the central highlands of Kenya. It was found that although 91% of households using calliandra fodder were male headed, in 89% of these households females were responsible for manag- ing calliandra. A similar scenario was observed in Uganda by Nyeko et al. (2004) whereby in over 80% of households with calliandra, women were involved in management.
